newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says FDI hit $235.3 mln in Jan-May.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says FDI hit $235.3 mln in Jan-May.

text.p: Foreign direct equity investment into the Philippines in the first five months of the year was $235.3 million, the central bank said on Monday.
This brought the cumulative level by the end of May to $7.6 billion.
Cumulative net portfolio foreign inflows reached $666 million by July 11, the central bank said.

The increases in foreign direct investment were in chemcials and chemical products, transport equipment, business services and construction. Last year, the big investments were in banks and other financial institutions, machinery, real estate and electricity.
It noted an increase in equity investments from Switzerland and Australia, with both surpassing their total in 1996.
Germany and Singapore also showed increased interest.
By far the largest overall investor remains the U.S. followed by Japan and then Hong Kong.
